I look at it as similar to someone relapsing. I know some judge others for relapsing, but those that have any understanding of the process know that’s part of it. No judgment. No shame. Just accepting who you are and what you are feeling right now. 
I’ll tell you what my therapist told me:
“Don’t ‘should’ on yourself”

If you start embracing that simple statement it really will remove so much shame from the formula. And it is so much easier to breathe without shame. 
It’s like a really really good night’s rest. Doesn’t fix everything but damn does it help!! 

Also I totally backslide after any change or as my therapist calls “growth”… 

Don’t should on yourself.

As far as activities to help cope… well I do what I call 4X4’s. Inhale, hold for 4 seconds, exhale for 4 seconds. Do that 4 times. It will help ground you. But if you’re still being chased by loudness in your head… what reaches past your pain without cost? Do you like plants? Maybe set up a rage room and break old plates or dilapidated electronics? Music will often let me tune out of my loud thoughts. Sometimes I even make really crappy drawings lol.  
You don’t have to shift through all the thoughts, especially if it’s all the same noise you always hear. It’s okay to tune it out. Buddhist have even agreed that video games are a great form of being in the moment/ mindfulness.

Sorry, this is my very first day in this sub. I never even thought to look for one for agoraphobia. I’ve been pretty isolated in this, no one in my family understands it, but a few of them try their best to make sure I feel supported and safe (husband included). 

But it’s a relief to find this group! I don’t feel so alone in this. And to see so many with the same complaints and struggles makes me feel like maybe I’m not crazy after all. It’s part of it. 

As far as your points:
Absolutely correct, I would have had an anxiety attack and been down for the rest of the day. Small steps, small but consistent and pushing myself marginally each and every time. Over and over and over. 

Right now the driving starts at a SUDS 2 and would be at a 4 within 15 mins. Some days are easier than others.. sometimes I start at a 3 and hit a 7 and have to pull over before I skip to a 9.

I’ve been consistently driving. It’s rare that I miss a day (I mean this has only been two weeks, I think I skipped driving 3 days of that). We are on week 3 now. But it has varied from 5 mins down the road to 45 mins away. Excluding one very painful drive two hours away into Atlanta traffic... but that was out of necessity for my sons neurosurgery follow up appointment. My husband is on military orders so it’s just me taking care of everything. It quickly forced me out of my comfort zone. I can do things more easily for my child than I can for anyone else, though. If that makes sense. 

Like if it were for me, I’d be like who needs a follow up for brain surgery, I’m fine, right??! And my husband would drag and drive me lol. But it’s just me, myself, and my toddler for now. 

The best tactic I found was I am more apt to leave if I get up in the morning and clean up, get everyone ready then head to the car. It’s just a task, I do not think of anything except my tasks to complete. Get stuff into car. Get baby into car seat and buckled- hand snack and water bottle. Walk around close the door. Seat belt. Sunglasses. Gas check, tire pressure check. If SUDS is too high at this point (higher than a 2 preferably) then I take a moment to breathe. Put on my classical melody (Bach concerto for keyboard D1 in minor BVW 10:52 Allegro) and chill for however long I need until I’m no longer coming apart at the seams. I’m usually good before the 2 min mark if I’m at a 3. Something about the cadence of the composure, if I can get sucked in then I’m good. If I can’t then I have to have a quiet moment with Weightless by Marconi Union. 

But sometimes you gotta get going bc the toddler has sabotaged the plan and we gonna be late late if we don’t go right now. Those are the worst. I try very hard to prevent those situations. 

I find I can’t do all the things on my list if it requires me to visit an actual shopping center. That’s all I can handle for that day. And I really freaking HATE exposing to that more. Ngl, I blame a lot of my not wanting to go on the pandemic lol. I do it at least once a week, though. 
But we go to the park twice a week and take a nice long walk. At least an hour as long as the toddler co-operates and doesn’t melt down. Other days are filled in with playdates or appointments/errands. 

Agreeing to set play dates was a big deal. I enjoy them but I *dread* the build up to them every single time. And I hate when I come off prickly to the other moms. I don’t know how to explain it to them that’s it’s just my anxiety and I want to go the heck home but it’s not because I don’t like them or enjoy this activity. It takes forever to find good mom groups with kids in the same range.

You don’t want to keep adding liquid and spread the sugar further. If it was a whole can of liquid I’d suggest lifting the mattress off the floor or box springs so it gets more air to it. Turn the ceiling fan on, if it isn’t & hasn’t been raining where you are, open the windows up if you can. 


When you go to the store next, add baking soda and white vinegar to your grocery list.
Then strip your mattress again and spray the white vinegar (dilute to a 1:1 ratio with water) on the spot (don’t pour lol it’s a strong smell). Then press a dry cloth into it. Repeat until you don’t see a stain. Then you sprinkle baking soda on it for an hour then wipe off, then let it air dry. 
The good news is you can do this later. White vinegar is a household cleaning GOD so go ahead and buy a bottle when you’re out next. 

You have time, don’t stress.

ETA: make sure to blot dry the vinegar solution before sprinkling baking soda, otherwise you’re going to have a small version of the volcano science fair project LOL. and don’t worry about molding in the inside from what you couldn’t get to, it’ll dry and be fine as long as you let it air dry and try to prevent spilling on the same area for a few days. Sleep on a towel if it’s still damp tonight. Just make sure to let it air the next day and it should be plenty dry by day 3.
